title: Unverified key

patterns: OP_DEPTH OP_0NOTEQUAL OP_NOTIF around a key
<key> CHECKSIG DROP with an empty signature
a 32-byte tapscript key that never has to verify

note: The hole in Knots #422. A pubkey is treated as real because CHECKSIG sits beside it, even when that check never succeeds: the opcode is in a branch guarded by OP_DEPTH, or it runs on an empty signature and the failure is dropped. Fourteen fake keys in a 1-of-15 then pass as ordinary multisig. SFS-5 counts 33-byte keys in a multisig and does not ask whether a signature verified. SFS-6 is a branch that constants make unreachable. This sidecar does not run the script, so this row is a name and the check is not written. Knots #470, by LionThunderFingers, recounts after the script runs and credits a key only when a signature verified against it.
